You could try some of the XLA flags defined here: https://github.com/openxla/xla/blob/c53c0a4f1564b87850e527ae16ed6f58e34218c0/xla/xla.proto#L504

In particular, `XLA_FLAGS=--xla_gpu_executable_terminate_timeout_seconds=N` seems like it could do what you're asking for.

issue.body:
### Description

I am running a very big sharded matrix (across 8 GPUs) through a somewhat complex jitted function. When the matrix is on the smaller side, everything works without any issues. When the matrix gets bigger, however, I get the following messages:
```
2025-02-25 18:35:03.087491: E external/xla/xla/service/rendezvous.cc:38] This thread has been waiting for `first call to collective operation 1; run_id=-1615834494` for 20 seconds and may be stuck. Expected 8 threads to join the rendezvous, but not all of them arrived on time.
2025-02-25 18:35:03.350158: E external/xla/xla/service/rendezvous.cc:38] This thread has been waiting for `first call to collective operation 1; run_id=-1615834494` for 20 seconds and may be stuck. Expected 8 threads to join the rendezvous, but not all of them arrived on time.
2025-02-25 18:35:08.111889: E external/xla/xla/service/rendezvous.cc:38] This thread has been waiting for `first call to collective operation 1; run_id=-1615834494` for 20 seconds and may be stuck. Expected 8 threads to join the rendezvous, but not all of them arrived on time.
2025-02-25 18:35:43.087819: E external/xla/xla/service/rendezvous.cc:50] Termination timeout for `first call to collective operation 1; run_id=-1615834494` of 40 seconds exceeded. Exiting to ensure a consistent program state. Expected 8 threads to join the rendezvous, but not all of them arrived on time.
2025-02-25 18:35:43.350371: E external/xla/xla/service/rendezvous.cc:50] Termination timeout for `first call to collective operation 1; run_id=-1615834494` of 40 seconds exceeded. Exiting to ensure a consistent program state. Expected 8 threads to join the rendezvous, but not all of them arrived on time.
[1]    623688 segmentation fault (core dumped)  TF_CUDNN_DETERMINISTIC=1 TF_DETERMINISTIC_OPS=1 XLA_FLAGS= =false =off =  -m
```
This happens about 95% of the time - if I just rerun it, the script sometimes runs without error. I have a feeling that I just need to increase the timeout duration somehow, but I couldn't find any information about how to do that (or whether it's possible).
